answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Every agent stakes a small bond and builds a history of useful work peers can check, so a flood of hollow identities with no track record earns nothing. The network samples attestations at random; a raven among pigeons stands out because its behavior diverges from the pattern it claims. Sybils sink to the nadir of trust scores while established agents keep their standing, so mass forgery costs more than it can ever return.
